name: Kaqchikel, Eastern
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). Es invariable en el proceso de derivación. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce función distintiva. A continuación se subrayan las sílabas donde hay acento.
new_statements.translation: The stress pattern in all varieties of the Kaqchikel language is fixed; its function is demarcative and its position is the final syllable (oxytone / last-syllable stress). It is invariable in the process of derivation. For that reason it need not be written, because it is predictable and has no distinctive function. Below, the syllables bearing stress are underlined.
new_statements.citation: Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel (ALMG); investigadores Juan Esteban Ajsivinac Sian, Lolmay Pedro Oscar García Matzar, Martín Chacach Cutzal, Ixkusamil Estela Alonzo Guaján. 2004. Gramática descriptiva del idioma maya Kaqchikel: Rutzijoxik rucholik ri Kaqchikel ch'ab'äl. Chimaltenango: Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel, Academia de Lenguas Mayas de Guatemala.
new_statements.locator: Fonología, section 'Acento', printed p.55 (p.59; page render), with fn.48 'Datos de la Variación Dialectal del Idioma Kaqchikel de la CLK, parte morfológica'; exceptions pp.56-57
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: opened (printed p.55, section 'Acento', running head FONOLOGÍA). The passage is there word for word: 'El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). Es invariable en el proceso de derivación. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce función distintiva. A continuación se subrayan las sílabas donde hay acento.' Footnote 48 reads 'Datos de la Variación Dialectal del Idioma Kaqchikel de la CLK, parte morfológica.' The example list (nupatz'an, patän, kumätz, tukur, qitzij, poqolaj, qulaj, saqb'äch, raxq'ab', xuk'äm pe, ach-'ajmak, musmül)…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the last syllable of the word in every variety of Kaqchikel; it is fixed, non-contrastive and stays final under derivation (examples p.55: nupatz'án, patän, kumätz, tukúr, qitzíj, poqoláj, quláj, saqb'äch, raxq'ab', xuk'ám pe, ach-'ajmák, musmül). OKMA 1997 p.20 adds that enclitics attached to verbs and statives attract the stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned by ALMG 2004. Bennett 2018 (Glossa 3(1):67, fn.7): 'Secondary stress has never been reported for Kaqchikel'.
new_statements.exceptions: ALMG 2004 p.56: (a) penultimate stress 'no es muy común en la mayoría de variantes', in a few native words (wakïx 'cow', tukur 'owl', tata, nana, b'alam, anxa, janila) and Spanish loans (anma, paxa, alb'ertix, xalma); (b) 'acento en sílaba pesada' in 'muy pocas palabras' only in Santa María de Jesús, Antigua Guatemala, Parramos, San Bartolomé Milpas Altas and Magdalena Milpas Altas; p.57 diphthong loans in Santa María de Jesús and Alotenango. None of the Eastern towns is among the exceptional variants. OKMA 1997 p.21: Spanish loans keep paroxytone/proparoxytone stress (kaxa, xara, anma); native nana, tata first-syllable; Comalapa janila. Chacach Cutzal 1999 p.171-172 lists the same paroxytone set (nána, táta, janíla, ánxa, ánima, káxa, xálma, xíla).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: 'la sílaba final de la palabra (radical, derivada o compuesta)' (OKMA 1997 p.20); invariant under derivation (ALMG 2004); enclitics on verbs/statives take the stress (OKMA). Phrase level: 'in phrases, the primary stress falls on the last word' (Brown, Maxwell & Little 2006:138, quoted in Nelson 2020). Data basis is the CLK dialect-variation survey of many towns including San Juan Sacatepéquez, San Pedro Sacatepéquez, San Raymundo and Chuarrancho; Bennett 2016 (Lang. & Ling. Compass 10:495) and Berinstein 1979 (Patzicía speakers, instrumental) agree on fixed final stress.
new_statements.identity_note: kaqc1273 is a Glottolog bookkeeping code for the retired ISO 639-3 code [cke] 'Eastern Kaqchikel' (Ethnologue 15: 'Northwest of and near Guatemala City, San Juan Sacatepéquez'; 100,000 speakers, 1998 SIL; NT 1986), merged into Kaqchikel [cak] (kaqc1270) by ISO CR 2008-053 on 2009-01-16. No description specific to the Eastern variety exists in anything opened or in any bibliographic record seen; the only Eastern-specific primary material found online is Kaufman's 1971 PLFM dialect questionnaire for San Juan Sacatepéquez (handwritten wordlist, no prose). The quoted statement is at Kaqchikel language level: ALMG 2004 asserts it 'en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel' on the CLK dialect-variation data, whose sample points include the Eastern towns San Juan Sacatepéquez, San Raymundo (printed pp.21, 30), San Pedro Sacatepéquez (pp.21, 41, 42) and Chuarrancho (pp.21, 24, 52); the marginal heavy-syllable pattern it reports (p.56) is confined to five non-Eastern towns. by our rule that each source is filed under the language's current Glottolog code (a retired code does not make a separate language) the catalog entry belongs under kaqc1270 (Kaqchikel), not as a separate kaqc1273 entity.
